subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk get its own opt-in STT backend boundary, and should the first implementation bridge finalized audio to `tools.media.audio` or use a separate native/provider contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but implementing it changes native app UX, provider routing, credential handling, private-network behavior, and fallback semantics; automation cannot choose those contracts safely.

options.title: Design PTT batch backend seam
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a final-text batch backend boundary for PTT, and align credentials/network/fallback behavior with existing provider and media-audio controls.

options.title: Fold into broader custom ASR design
options.body: Treat this issue as a child of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 and wait for one native ASR/STT contract that covers multiple platform voice flows.

options.title: Defer native custom STT
options.body: Keep native PTT Apple Speech-only until maintainers decide configurable ASR endpoints are supportable for the macOS app.

recommendation.title: Design PTT batch backend seam
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a final-text batch backend boundary for PTT, and align credentials/network/fallback behavior with existing provider and media-audio controls.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest inspected history signal is in the native macOS voice files and adjacent media-understanding refactors, and the issue timeline already mentions this owner area.
